- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.16+ over recent days), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in next period — cap forecast peak at +1.5–2.0% above prior high or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model frequently underestimates upward momentum — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if recent 3–5 days show upward trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward drift, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment in next period if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in late period — increase forecast variance by 0.3–0.7% in final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “negative → neutral” transitions, model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual turning point if sentiment shifts upward.
